idiom_name: explicit document struct with typed fields (no view layer)
implementation_notes: The pattern's payoff, type-safe views over a property map without losing the flexibility of a dynamic language, cannot be delivered in C: there are no interfaces with default implementations to hang views on, stored values carry no runtime type information (a void* is a promise, not a check), and a cast mistake is undefined behaviour rather than a caught exception. What remains is a hash map of void* plus a tagging and casting convention - every cost of the pattern and none of its guarantee. Where the document really is dynamic (a JSON payload, plugin-provided settings) keep it at the boundary: parse it with a serialisation library (cJSON, jansson), read the fields you need through that library's typed accessors, and copy them into an ordinary struct that the rest of the code uses.
pitfalls: void*-valued property bags carry no runtime type information: reading a value through the wrong struct type is undefined behaviour, and no sanitizer is guaranteed to catch it.
cJSON owns its tree and jansson reference-counts json_t, so pointers borrowed out of the document dangle after cJSON_Delete/json_decref - copy into native structs before releasing it.
String keys and no schema: a typo is a silent NULL and must be checked at every single access.
alternative: Declare an explicit struct per document type with typed fields and accessor functions; use a JSON library (cJSON, jansson) only at the serialization boundary and convert the loose tree into that struct once.
